questions.question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

Statements:

Some Circular Saws are Trowels.

Some Trowels are Power Saws.

Conclusions:

I: Some Circular Saws are Power Saws.

II: No Circular Saws are Power Saws.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cad0a1384c206bdf8b3ede276d8b08ea0c9f563c583564d0f134a45027946d66.png] 

Conclusions:

I Some Circular Saws are Power Saws → Does not follow (As some Circular Saws are Trowels and some Trowels are Power Saws. So it is possible but not definite.)

II No Circular Saws are Power Saws → does not follow (As some Circular Saws are Trowels and some Trowels are Power Saws. As no direct relation is given between Circular Saws and Power Saws, therefore it true.)

Thus, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All soaps are gels.

All soaps are conditioners.

Conclusions:

(I) Some gels are conditioners.

(II) All conditioners are soaps.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All soaps are gels.

All soaps are conditioners.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ac2741a4e7e14094c76939a4883602d8b9546cfdf014cd1caf1abf0ba0014ac.png] 

Conclusions:

**(I) Some gels are conditioners:**

Since all **Soaps** are **Gels** (Statement 1) and all **Soaps** are **Conditioners** (Statement 2), the elements that are Soaps (the common part) must be both Gels and Conditioners.

Therefore, the area of overlap between Gels and Conditioners is non-empty.

**Conclusion (I) logically follows.**

**(II) All conditioners are soaps:**

This conclusion is the converse of Statement 2 ("All Soaps are Conditioners").

In a universal affirmative statement (**All A are B**), the converse (**All B are A**) is **not necessarily true**. There may be conditioners that are not soaps (the part of the Conditioners set outside the Soaps set).

**Conclusion (II) does not follow.**

Thus, **Only conclusion (I) follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the pair in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following pairs.

(Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

12, 146

8, 66
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: Second number = (First number)² + 2

12, 146

⇒ 12² = 144
144 + 2 = **146**

8, 66

⇒ 8² = 64
64 + 2 = **66**

Now, checking the options:

Option 1) 6, 34

⇒ 6² + 2 = 36 + 2 = 38

**Option 2) 11, 123**

**⇒ 11² + 2 = 121 + 2 =** **123**

Option 3) 7, 49

⇒ 7² + 2 = 49 + 2 = 51

Option 4) 4, 66

⇒ 4² + 2 = 16 + 2 = 18

Hence, the correct option is "Option 2"
